title: Short Stuff: Humpty Dumpty
summary: Short Stuff episode on the origins and theories behind the nursery rhyme Humpty Dumpty. The hosts open with a tribute to Humpty Hump (Digital Underground rapper) who recently died, then cover how the rhyme was originally a riddle whose answer (an egg) was later assumed. They discuss the rhyme's earliest printed version with "four score men" in Juvenile Amusement by Samuel Arnold, theories that Humpty Dumpty was Richard III (linked to Shakespeare's portrayal and the Battle of Bosworth, where he reportedly fell from his horse Wall), Cardinal Wolsey (via the satire Punch), the 1803 Mother Goose's Melody appearance, Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass (1871) and John Tenniel's illustration that made Humpty an egg, and the idea that Humpty Dumpty was a strong drink of ale boiled with brandy. The episode ends with a mock cocktail recipe and sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and Humpty Hump tribute
segments.summary: The hosts open by remembering rapper Humpty Hump of Digital Underground, who recently died, and mention his 'Humpty Dance' and the track 'Risky Business'.

segments.title: Riddle origins and early rhyme versions
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the rhyme and say it was originally a riddle whose answer (an egg) was later forgotten. They note the 'four score men' version in Samuel Arnold's Juvenile Amusement, and that people began looking for hidden meanings after the original context was lost.

segments.title: Richard III theory
segments.summary: One theory holds Humpty Dumpty represents Richard III, whom Shakespeare depicted as a humpbacked toad. The hosts note Richard reigned about twenty-six months and was reportedly unfairly portrayed. He was the last English king to die in battle, at Bosworth, reportedly after falling from his horse Wall.

segments.title: Mother Goose's Melody and Cardinal Wolsey theory
segments.summary: The rhyme appears in Mother Goose's Melody (1803). The British satire Punch said Humpty symbolized Cardinal Wolsey, who failed to get a papal divorce for Henry VIII. The hosts doubt this, arguing a children's rhyme more likely refers to Richard III.

segments.title: Lewis Carroll and the egg image
segments.summary: Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass (1871) features Humpty Dumpty as a talking egg-like character, and John Tenniel's illustration showed him as an egg with arms, legs and pants. The hosts say this book fixed the egg image in popular imagination, and that its final line differs from the rhyme.

segments.title: Humpty Dumpty as a drink
segments.summary: Another theory says Humpty Dumpty was a drink, ale boiled with brandy, an early 1700s slang term that may relate to a strong beer called 'hum'. The hosts jokingly share a modern cocktail recipe.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the episode and note it is a production of iHeartRadio.
